title: Path Traversal in Static File Serving in ssr-prod.js
analysis:
In `ssr-prod.js`, the Polka HTTP server serves static files by directly concatenating user-controlled `req.url` with `'./dist/client'` and resolving the path using `path.resolve`:
```javascript
const file = path.resolve('./dist/client' + req.url);
```
There is no validation or containment check (e.g., verifying `file.startsWith(...)` or preventing directory traversal sequences). As a result, an attacker can supply directory traversal sequences (`..`) in `req.url` to escape the `./dist/client` directory and read arbitrary files on the filesystem.

Data path:
- Source: `req.url` from incoming HTTP request.
- Sanitization/Validation: None.
- Sink: `fs.createReadStream(file).pipe(res)`

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```http
GET /../../../../etc/passwd HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
```
This causes `path.resolve('./dist/client/../../../../etc/passwd')` to resolve to `/etc/passwd`. Because `/etc/passwd` exists, `fs.existsSync(file)` returns true and `fs.createReadStream(file).pipe(res)` streams the contents of `/etc/passwd` back in the HTTP response.
